A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete, readable 21-page DISRetrieval paper, including Appendices A–C. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical manuscript content; only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp and its link differ.

before.justification: v4 reports original retrieval and question-answering experiments on four datasets in Section 4, plus computational timing, retrieval-characteristic analyses, and sensitivity experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix C, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and computational timing measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3, Appendix A, and Algorithms 1–2 retain identical sentence-level discourse parsing, LLM node enhancement, tree integration, and structure-guided evidence retrieval procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use RST-DT with Chinese translation and evaluate QASPER, QuALITY, NarrativeQA, and MultiFieldQA-zh. The represented domains, languages, tasks, and test scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain flatten-chunk, flatten-sentence, RAPTOR, and Bisection. The LLM comparisons and retrieval variants also have identical membership; no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix B retain identical splits, sample counts, metrics, context lengths, model configurations, and preprocessing. The gold-evidence, full-document, ablation, and timing evaluation procedures also match.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix C retain the same evidence-context comparisons, retrieval-strategy ablations, parser-capability and LLM-scale studies, computational analyses, retrieval-granularity analyses, and Top-K and threshold sensitivity experiments.

E5.justification: Appendix C.1 retains sampling 10 documents per length range and reporting mean processing time with standard deviation. No repeated-run, seed, uncertainty-reporting, or statistical-estimation information changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted results, rankings, and reported findings match across the main text and appendices. For example, Table 3 retains DISRetrieval's 400-word-context F1 scores of 35.25 with GPT-4.1-mini and 29.54 with Deepseek-v3.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 and the formal descriptions in Section 3 and Appendix A are identical, including parser states, action probabilities, the training objective, and tree-construction definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning discourse-aware retrieval, benchmark performance, multi-granularity evidence selection, and cross-lingual robustness.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability arguments are unchanged. The Limitations section retains the same qualifications about parser quality, English/Chinese coverage, simple summarization thresholds, and evaluation metrics.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, model identifiers, prompts, GPU resources, parameter settings, and code/data access information are identical. The updated arXiv self-link only identifies the later paper version.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and citations throughout the appendices are unchanged. The positioning relative to semantic clustering, hierarchical retrieval, and previous discourse-based approaches is identical.

P1.justification: The first-page marginal stamp changes from arXiv v4 dated 14 January 2026 to v5 dated 7 May 2026. This is a limited identification-text update; manuscript wording, authors, headings, and organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9, Tables 1–8, algorithm displays, captions, and page layout are identical. Rendered pages match everywhere outside the updated first-page version/date text.

improvement.justification: v5 reproduces v4's scientific content, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, limitations, and presentation, including all appendices. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp and self-link has no meaningful effect on the paper's overall quality.
